The aperture is a regular N-sided polygon with apothem \(a\). As \(N \to \infty\), the polygon becomes a circle of radius \(a\). The far-field diffraction pattern of a circular aperture has minima at angles where \(J_1(ka \sin\theta) = 0\), with \(k = 2\pi/\lambda\). The first two zeros of \(J_1(x)\) are \(x_1 = 3.8317\) and \(x_2 = 7.0156\). Using the small-angle approximation \(\sin\theta \approx \theta\), the first minimum is at \(\theta_1 = 3.8317 \lambda / (2\pi a) \approx 0.610 \lambda / a\), and the second minimum is at \(\theta_2 = 7.0156 \lambda / (2\pi a) \approx 1.1165 \lambda / a\). The angular distance between them is \(\theta_2 - \theta_1 \approx 0.506 \lambda / a\).

Answer: A
